chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Sa'id al-A'raj who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the residue (of water) of the Jew and Christian, and he said: No.

key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيّ: The Christian (Nasrani) — used here in the jurisprudential sense of a member of the Christian faith
key_terms.الْيَهُودِيّ: The Jew — used here in the jurisprudential sense of a member of the Jewish faith
key_terms.سُؤْر: Su'r — the water or food remaining after a person has drunk or eaten from it; in fiqh, the su'r of a ritually impure person renders wudu invalid

ai.seo_question: Is the leftover water of a Jew or Christian ritually pure in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Sa'id al-A'raj asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) whether the water left over by Jews and Christians could be used for wudu (ritual ablution). The Imam's reply — a terse 'No' — establishes a ruling of ritual impurity (najasah) attributed to non-Muslims (ahl al-kitab) in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling reflects the early Shia legal position on the najasah of non-Muslims, a topic of significant scholarly discussion throughout Islamic history.
